title: Introduction to asg4nbashots
text: ’s compute shot accuracy year zone using built-helper function. can also manually create quick summary dplyr:
code: shot_zone_summary() library(dplyr) library(lubridate)  nba_shots |>   mutate(year = year(game_date)) |>   group_by(year) |>   summarise(     attempts = n(),     made = sum(shot_made_flag),     accuracy = made / attempts,     .groups = "drop"   )

what: Accuracy and expected points by distance
title: Introduction to asg4nbashots
code: library(ggplot2)  summary_df <- nba_shots |>   group_by(shot_distance) |>   summarise(     accuracy = mean(shot_made_flag),     expected_points = mean(shot_type * shot_made_flag),     .groups = "drop"   )  ggplot(summary_df, aes(shot_distance)) +   geom_point(aes(y = accuracy), color = "steelblue") +   geom_point(aes(y = expected_points), color = "red") +   labs(     title = "Accuracy and Expected Points by Distance",     x = "Distance (ft)",     y = "Average Accuracy / Expected Points"   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: Introduction to asg4nbashots

title: Using the Shiny App
text: left panel controls data shown tabs. Show Year Data (Overlay) Displays per-year points “Accuracy & Expected Points” tab (’ll see cloud faint dots per distance). Average Overall Years Shows pooled average curve across years (single dot per distance). Year slider neither two checkboxes active, slider filters app specific year. Season type Choose Regular Season, Playoffs, . Shot Outcome (Shot Location tab ) Filter Scored, Missed, . (Accuracy tab, enforced since accuracy/expected points require attempts makes.)

title: Using the Shiny App
text: ’ll see: Scatter shots transformed single offensive half (left-hand side). Red = scored, blue = missed. Darker areas = attempts. Reference lines mark baseline, half-court sidelines. use: Toggle Season type compare Playoffs vs Regular Season patterns. Use Shot Outcome focus scored-patterns missed-clusters. Switch Year (aggregate years) see historical changes.

title: Using the Shiny App
text: ’ll see: Black points = average shot accuracy distance (made / attempts). Red points = average expected points distance (mean(shot_type * shot_made_flag)), 3s count triple made. x-axis caps ~33 ft (≈ 400 , half court). Grey vertical markers show key distances (e.g., ~2.5 ft, ~22–29 ft). Typical stories look : close range (< 2.5 ft) highest accuracy. Mid-range (≈ 2.5–22 ft) maintains fairly steady accuracy. Long range (> 22 ft) accuracy drops, expected points can rise near 3-point line made shots worth 3. Good combos try: Average Overall Years , Show Year Data (Overlay) → clean, pooled curves. Turn Overlay → see per-year variability around pooled curve. Turn pick Year → one specific season.

title: Using the Shiny App
text: App won’t launch? Restart R try asg4nbashots::run_nbashots_app() . Long first load? ’s normal; dataset large. Later loads faster. Nothing appears / red error plot? Make sure least one Season type selected. Confusing results? Check whether ’ve enabled overlays versus pooled averages, chosen specific year.

what: Example: Accuracy and Expected Points by Distance
title: NBA Shot Data 1997–2020 Explorer
text: example illustrates calculate two common performance metrics: Accuracy: percentage made shots distance Expected points: average points scored per attempt, based shot success shot type (2 3-point)  blue points represent average shot accuracy distance, red points show expected points per attempt — capturing value longer shots 3-pointers become frequent.
code: library(dplyr) library(ggplot2)  # Compute accuracy and expected points by distance summary_df <- nba_shots %>%   group_by(shot_distance) %>%   summarise(     accuracy = mean(shot_made_flag),     expected_points = mean(shot_type * shot_made_flag),     .groups = "drop"   )  # Plot both metrics ggplot(summary_df, aes(x = shot_distance)) +   geom_point(aes(y = accuracy), color = "blue") +   geom_point(aes(y = expected_points), color = "red") +   scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 33), breaks = seq(0, 33, by = 2.5)) +   scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1.6), breaks = seq(0, 1.6, by = 0.2)) +   labs(     title = "Accuracy and Expected Points by Distance",     x = "Shot Distance (feet)",     y = "Average Accuracy / Expected Points"   ) +   theme_minimal()

title: NBA Shot Data, 1997–2020 — nba_shots
text: Detailed shot-level data 4.7 million NBA attempts 1997 2020, including shot type, distance, court zones, outcome, season context analysis shot selection efficiency, interactive exploration via Shiny.

title: NBA Shot Data, 1997–2020 — nba_shots
text: tibble 4,729,512 rows 11 variables: action_type factor — specific shot action (e.g., Jump Shot, Layup, Dunk). shot_distance integer — distance feet. shot_zone_basic factor — broad shot zone (e.g., Restricted Area, Mid-Range, Left Corner 3). shot_zone_area factor — court area (Left Side, Center, Right Side). shot_zone_range factor — distance category (e.g., <8 ft, 8–16 ft, 16–24 ft, 24+ ft). x_location integer — x-coordinate court. y_location integer — y-coordinate court. shot_type integer — shot value (2 3). shot_made_flag integer — 1 made, 0 missed. game_date Date — YYYY-MM-DD. season_type factor — season category (Regular Season, Playoffs).

title: NBA Shot Data, 1997–2020 — nba_shots
text: Public “NBA Shot Data 1997–2020” https://data.world/sportsvizsunday/june-2020-nba-shots-1997-2019; inspired Stand-Maths' video “analysed 4,678,387 NBA shots” (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yh5c3duQQ1w). Differences total rows (~4.7M vs 4.68M cited) likely reflect source compilation filtering. cleaned processed data-raw/nba_shots.R.
